summary: How the leading liberal newspapers of Italy, Weimar Germany and the United States, notably La Stampa, the Ullstein house and The New York Times, downplayed fascist violence, sided against the left and buried the Holocaust between 1919 and 1945.

evidence.note: Italian section starts at the end of WWI in 1918 and runs to the March on Rome
1920 factory occupations and Red Guards dismissed by the liberal Italian papers
fascists destroy left-wing papers while liberal press excuses squadristi violence
pivot to the Ullstein publishing house, Weimar's largest liberal press
Ullstein backs coalition with the Nazis; Tempo pushes consumption in 1932
Part 2 turns to the US press and its fondness for Mussolini and Hitler
NYT Berlin correspondent Birchall downplays Nazi persecution in 1933
Ochs and Sulzberger avoid covering Nazi persecution of Jews to look impartial
NYT front-page treatment of the Holocaust through the end of the war in 1945
Dorothy Thompson's 1941 Harper's essay closes the historical narrative
framed by present-day NYT and Washington Post conduct under the same families

notes: Story is about institutions, so primary subjects are Ullstein and the NYT and roles are empty; La Stampa stands in for the Italian section (L'Illustrazione Italiana in keywords). Long present-day segments (Gaza coverage, Trump, Vance) are comparisons and do not extend covered_span, but the framing that the same media families still run US papers sets reaches_present. No content warning: the Holocaust is discussed as press coverage, not described in detail.
